subject: Mid-window OKR steer: scope clarifications, runway model, and dependency asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-window OKR steer: scope clarifications, runway model, and dependency asks

Team —

Quick mid-window check. I reviewed the Q3 runway model (attached) against current deliverables and re-ran a few variant assumptions. High-level summary and asks below — aiming to lock decisions by end of week so the QBR deck reflects committed scope.

1) Status & risk highlights
- Analytics-inference latency OKR: on track for baseline perf, but model quantization work is ~3w behind due to kernel validation. This primarily impacts cost-per-token improvements.
- Redwood Console rollout for large tenants: feature-complete, but product docs + self-serve onboarding are only ~40% done. Docs gap is the gating dependency for two mid-market account pilots (Acme, Brightline).
- Dedicated capacity autoscale policy: needs an infra EVAL before we sign off on SLOs; Legal requested a short data-retention exception (see dependency roster).

2) Proposed re-scope (to be ratified)
- Option A (minimal): Defer advanced quantization to Q4, keep latency OKR as a stability target; ship Console GA for small/medium tenants first.
- Option B (ambitious): Keep quantization in Q3, shift 20% of Console docs effort to an external technical writer contract (cost ~ $12k) to unblock pilots.

3) Concrete asks (owners + timelines)
- Markus: confirm kernel validation ETA or provide rollback criteria by EOD Thu (owner: markus_klein).
- Laura: flag any customer commitments that require Option B and share a prioritized pilot list (owner: laura_bennett) by Thu COB.
- Naomi: advise if leadership can approve a $12k contractor line for docs (owner: naomi_feldman) — decision by Fri morning so we can issue PO.
- Vanessa: coordinate with CloudPartner (Tomas) to see if a temporary capacity patch is possible to meet pilot SLAs (owner: vanessa_ortiz) — ping Tomas today.

4) Attachments & artifacts
- Q3_runway_model.csv (attached): sensitivity scenarios for margin, latency, and time-to-GA.
- dependency_roster_v2.pdf (attached): cross-team dependency matrix and suggested owners.

Ask: please reply with a single-line readout: APPROVE-OPTION-A or APPROVE-OPTION-B or REQUEST-CONCURRENCE + any blockers. If you need me to call a 15-min steer, I can schedule for Thu morning.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3_runway_model.csv (spreadsheet), dependency_roster_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-window OKR steer: scope clarifications, runway model, and dependency asks

Karthik —

Brief readout: kernel validation is longer than I hoped. Root cause: an edge case in the fused attention kernel when sequence-length > 8k (rare but repros on our stress bench). Team estimate: 2w to harden + 1w for regression testing.

Rollback criteria I can commit to if needed:
- Disable the new fused kernel and fall back to baseline kernels (expected ~8-12% latency penalty, known behavior).
- If we hit any production perf regression > 15% on the pilot, we auto-roll back the kernel change and open an incident.

Given that, I lean toward Option A unless leadership wants to accept the 3w risk and fund parallel QA velocity. APPROVE-OPTION-A (tentative).

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Inference Engineering
